how.title: How It Works
how.intro: CropDoc GB uses a deep-learning model that learned leaf-disease patterns from thousands of labelled leaf photos.
how.step1: Upload or capture a clear photo of one affected leaf
how.step2: The AI looks for disease patterns and shows where it looked (heatmap)
how.step3: Get the likely disease and general guidance
how.tip: For best results, take close-up photos of single leaves in good daylight.

field.title: Field Intelligence
field.lead: Why do AI models trained on clean lab photos fail on real field photos, and what helps? Every number below is loaded from a result file; missing results are marked PENDING.
field.story1: Lab photos (PlantVillage) show one leaf on a plain background. Field photos have soil, hands, other leaves, shadows and phone cameras. A model can learn shortcuts from the lab background instead of the disease itself.
field.story2: We measure the gap honestly: first on public real-world photos (PlantDoc, from the web), and later on photos from Gilgit-Baltistan fields.
field.contributeLead: Help build the Gilgit-Baltistan test set. Photos are stored only on this computer, in a local inbox folder, and are used only after an expert checks the label.

about.title: About CropDoc GB
about.what: CropDoc GB is a student research project: a free plant-disease scanner for farmers in Gilgit-Baltistan, and an honest study of the gap between lab-trained AI and real fields.
about.dataBody: Trained on PlantVillage lab photos (38 classes, 14 crops). Photos of the same leaf were kept in one split to avoid inflated accuracy. Real field photos look different, so accuracy in the field is lower.
about.notReplacement: CropDoc GB is not a replacement for agronomists or agriculture extension officers. It gives general guidance only, not a diagnosis.
about.privacy: Privacy: no accounts, no tracking. Photos and history stay on this computer; location data (EXIF/GPS) is removed from every photo.
about.licensesBody: Leaf photos: PlantVillage (CC BY-SA 3.0). Real-world test photos: PlantDoc (CC BY 4.0). Pretrained weights: timm (Apache 2.0).

live.subtitle: Point the camera at one leaf. The answer appears on screen as the model sees it.
live.pointAtLeaf: Point at one leaf inside the box
live.holdSteadyBody: The model needs two matching frames before it shows an answer. Keep the leaf still inside the box.
live.moveCloser: Not sure: move closer, one leaf only
live.noLeaf: No supported leaf in the box
live.noFrame: No camera picture yet. Wait for the camera to start.
live.speedHelp: Time from camera to answer for the last frame, measured on this device.
live.tip1: Hold the phone about a hand-span from ONE leaf.
live.tip2: Fit the leaf inside the box; keep other leaves out.
live.tip3: Hold still for a second until the box turns green.
live.tip4: Tap the round button to save a full report with the heatmap.
live.tipLight: Daylight without harsh shadows works best.
live.problem.insecure.title: Live camera needs a secure link
live.problem.insecure.body: Phones allow the live camera only on https:// addresses. You can still take a photo now, or start the app in phone mode on your computer (see below).
live.problem.unsupported.title: This browser has no live camera
live.problem.unsupported.body: Open the app in Chrome, Edge or Safari, or take a photo instead.
live.problem.denied.title: Camera permission is blocked
live.problem.denied.body: Allow the camera for this site (tap the lock icon in the address bar → Permissions → Camera), then try again. Or take a photo instead.
live.problem.not_found.title: No camera found
live.problem.not_found.body: Connect a webcam or use a phone. You can also take or choose a photo.
live.problem.busy.title: Camera is busy
live.problem.busy.body: Another app (video call, camera app) is using the camera. Close it and try again.
live.problem.other.title: Camera could not start
live.problem.other.body: Try again, or take a photo instead.
